A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the TCR Vbeta repertoire of penicilloylspecific T cells is rather heterogeneous, and the TCR Vbetas are not a marker for a certain hapten specificity, but rather a marker for the cross-reactivity of T cells.
the cross-reactive T cells are characterized by a heterogenous T cell receptor repertoire and the monospecific T cells by a restricted T cell receptor usage.
the T cell response to beta-lactams is highly heterogeneous, as the T cell repertoire is not restricted to one epitope.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the T cells in penicillin allergic patients are not monospecific, but can recognize a broad range of beta-lactams.
the T cell response to penicillin is highly heterogeneous and that this is reflected by the TCR repertoire.
the molecular mechanisms of the immune response to beta-lactams are more complex than expected.
